why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests the `<path>:<line>: ` shape, 1-based numbering, skipped blank lines, the torn last line and exit codes 0 and 1, all named in expect line 1. "Exactly one line" follows from "every row that is not valid JSON": an extra line would report a valid row. Check 2 tests only exit 2 and non-empty stderr. Check 3 tests the exported lint, the array shape and line/error, and an empty array for clean input, which the meaning of "returning [{ line, error }]" covers. Check 4 accepts "node --test (optionally with args)" and requires the listed cases. Its "tests pass" condition is backed by line 6's green npm test. Check 6 follows "one PR", the Closes line and "green". The stricter items (shebang and executable bit, CRLF, lockfile, stdout/stderr separation, phantom trailing-newline error) all sit under Advisory.
